articles.title: AI Agents are Vulnerable to Radicalization
articles.description:
arXiv:2609.38296v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) can influence people's beliefs, yet little is known about whether and how they can manipulate each other. To investigate this, we simulate conversations between two agents: a target LLM that role-plays a human persona based on demographic and psychological attributes, and an influencer LLM that aims to make the target's beliefs more extreme. articles.title: Examining Variation in How Guided AI Tutors Resolve Student Impasses
articles.description:
arXiv:2609.38346v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: When a student is stuck, a tutor faces the assistance dilemma: help given too early can hinder productive struggle, while help withheld too long leaves the student in a frustrating, persistent impasse (i.e., wheel spinning). Generative AI tutors increasingly use guardrails restricting answer-giving, yet little is known about how such tutors behave once an impasse persists. We analyze 20,462 student turns from 1,260 authentic sessions with a guided
articles.title_zh: Examining Variation in How Guided AI Tutors Resolve Student Impasses

articles.title: MetaPersona: Task-Grounded Synthetic Populations from Empirical Social Science
articles.description:
arXiv:2609.38392v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Personas used to seed LLM social simulations face a cold-start problem: existing methods lack a principled basis for deciding which attributes to include and how to assign their values. As a result, synthetic populations may misrepresent the demographic composition, latent attributes, and dependency structure that shape downstream behavior. articles.title_zh: MetaPersona: Task-Grounded Synthetic Populations from Empirical Social Science

articles.title: Can an AI Agent Rediscover a Blaschke-Curve Invariant?
articles.description:
arXiv:2609.38369v1 Announce Type: new

articles.title: AREX-2: Advancing Self-Improving Agents through Long-Horizon Reflective Tasks
articles.description:
arXiv:2609.38288v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We present AREX-2, an effort to advance the self-improving capability of LLM agents, which we define as the ability to iteratively refine a solution at test time. This ability rests on two complementary capabilities: reflection, which produces a solution better than the current one, and long-horizon execution, which keeps the iteration effective over many rounds. articles.title_zh: AREX-2: Advancing Self-Improving Agents through Long-Horizon Reflective Tasks

articles.title: Beyond Mode Collapse: Generating Diverse Synthetic Expert Conversations via Generative Flow Networks
articles.description:

articles.title: A Competing-Hazards Systematization of Loss of Control in Autonomous Agents
articles.description:
arXiv:2609.38411v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Leading AI developers have reported agents acting beyond their approved limits, which a United Nations panel described as an early warning of loss of human control. articles.title_zh: A Competing-Hazards Systematization of Loss of Control in Autonomous Agents

articles.title: CARAT: Do Materials LLMs Reason or Recite?
articles.description:
arXiv:2609.38340v1 Announce Type: new
